title: Delegated Approval & Escalation Playbook for Model Rollouts
creator: Maya Singh
description: Goal: Define a concrete, auditable approval and escalation playbook for model production rollouts that supports delegated sign-offs, separation-of-duty, and automatic rollback/escalation for canary, A/B and shadow traffic use-cases. This ticket covers policy, RBAC mappings, audit log schema, approval expiry rules, and on-call escalation for emergency rollbacks. Scope excludes implementation of runtime rollback mechanics (tracked separately under ENG-2034) but must specify trigger thresholds and required attestation steps for any rollback action.
comments: 2026-03-02 - Kickoff: aligned with SRE and Security. Agreed on separation-of-duty: deployer != approver for P0 rollouts.
2026-03-04 - Decision: delegated approvers allowed for low-risk A/B experiments (<=5% traffic) with automated metric gates; high-risk canaries require two approvers (PM + SRE).
2026-03-06 - PM review feedback: add explicit approval expiry (default 72h) and re-attestation requirement after any model config change.
2026-03-09 - Security review notes: include KMS-signed approval tokens, non-repudiation header in audit logs, and 7-year retention for regulated customers behind Private deployments.
2026-03-11 - DevOps input: must surface rollback reason and triggering metric in console and include a link to incident runbook when an auto-rollback occurs.
2026-03-13 - Draft ready for design pass; design to propose UI copy and minimal confirmation UX for delegated approvers.
2026-03-13 - Linked artifacts: RFC and draft policy attached. Next: tabletop with SRE on 2026-03-17.
acceptance_criteria: Playbook doc describing role mappings (Deployer, Approver, Emergency Approver, SRE Oncall) and permitted actions per role exists in Confluence.
RBAC spec (mapping to Console and API) with least-privilege default checked into platform repo and PR reviewed by Security.
Audit log schema and retention policy documented; sample logs produced by a simulated rollout recorded in the audit bucket.
Approval expiry behavior implemented as documented (default 72 hours) and configurable per project.
Auto-rollback triggers defined and validated with SLO owners; tabletop test executed with on-call and results documented.
rollback_triggers: Error rate increase > 5% absolute (and > 2x relative) within first 15 minutes of canary traffic for traffic-weight >= 1%
99th percentile latency breach above SLO by > 30% sustained for 5 minutes
Degradation in model output quality as measured by golden prompt regression score drop of >= 4 points on the approved eval set
Manual emergency rollback invoked by SRE Oncall or Approver when incident runbook determines systemic failure
Data-governance indicator: unexpected PII leak detected by content-scan policy
rbac_roles: Deployer: can schedule rollouts, attach rollout config, cannot approve P0/P1 rollouts
Approver: product/PM role; can approve canaries up to 10% if one Approver + automatic gating in place
Release Approver: senior PM or Release Eng; required for production canaries >= 10% or P0 changes
SRE Oncall: emergency approver and escalation contact; can trigger immediate rollback
Auditor: read-only access to full audit trail and approval artifacts
audit_requirements: Every approval must emit an immutable, KMS-signed token recorded in the audit log with approver id, role, timestamp, expiry, and scope (model id, version, routes)
Rollback events must include trigger metric snapshot, associated trace id(s), and link to console incident ticket
Audit logs for Private deployments support HSM-backed signatures and export to customer SIEM via syslog or S3
Retention default: 1 year for hosted; 7 years for regulated Private customers (configurable per customer)
followups: Design: create minimal approval UX and review copy for delegated approver confirmation (DES-4123).
Engineering: implement RBAC enforcement hooks in Console and API and add approval token generation (ENG-2034).
SRE: schedule tabletop test simulating auto-rollback flows with on-call on 2026-03-17.
Security: finalize KMS/HSM signing integration and verify non-repudiation requirements.
PM: prepare customer-facing runbook and release notes describing the new controls.
